MTD calendar

MTD calendar: when Making Tax Digital applies to you

Which dates apply to your business

Find your business type, then follow the link in each column to its dates. Making Tax Digital for Income Tax covers sole traders and landlords registered for Self Assessment, so a limited company is outside it. Partnerships have no date yet. A taxi or private hire driver, and a sole trader with employees, follow the sole trader rules.

Dates

Each entry shows the words from the gov.uk page it comes from and the day we read that page.

  1. 1 April 2022VAT: every VAT-registered business

    All VAT-registered businesses use Making Tax Digital for VAT, whatever their turnover. Your first VAT period starting on or after 1 April 2022 is the first one under the rule.

    Relevant for: every business type in the table, once it is VAT registered.

    Businesses need to have signed up to Making Tax Digital for their first VAT return starting on or after 1 April 2022.

    gov.uk/government/news/making-tax-digital-for-vat-is-coming-are-you-ready Retrieved 30 October 2026

  2. 18 November 2025Companies House: director and PSC identity verification

    Identity verification is a legal requirement for directors and for people with significant control (PSCs). A director gives the personal code with the company's next confirmation statement. A PSC verifies and gives the personal code within a 14 day period that depends on the PSC's situation.

    Relevant for: Owner-managed company with one director, Property company, Small company.

    You will need to provide your Companies House personal code as part of your company’s next confirmation statement.

    gov.uk/guidance/when-you-need-to-verify-your-identity-for-companies-house Retrieved 24 October 2026

    Identity verification is now a legal requirement.

    gov.uk/guidance/when-you-need-to-verify-your-identity-for-companies-house Retrieved 24 October 2026

    PSCs must verify their identity and provide their Companies House personal code.

    gov.uk/guidance/when-you-need-to-verify-your-identity-for-companies-house Retrieved 24 October 2026

  3. 6 April 2026Income Tax: qualifying income over £50,000

    Sole traders and landlords with qualifying income over £50,000 in the 2024 to 2025 tax year use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.

    Relevant for: Sole trader, Taxi and private hire driver, Landlord, Sole trader with employees.

    £50,000 for the 2024 to 2025 tax year, you should’ve started using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026

    gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 30 October 2026

    you’re a sole trader or a landlord registered for Self Assessment

    gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 24 October 2026

  4. 6 April 2027Income Tax: qualifying income over £30,000

    The rule reaches qualifying income over £30,000 in the 2025 to 2026 tax year.

    Relevant for: Sole trader, Taxi and private hire driver, Landlord, Sole trader with employees.

    £30,000 for the 2025 to 2026 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2027

    gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 30 October 2026

    you’re a sole trader or a landlord registered for Self Assessment

    gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 24 October 2026

  5. 6 April 2028Income Tax: qualifying income over £20,000

    The rule reaches qualifying income over £20,000 in the 2026 to 2027 tax year.

    Relevant for: Sole trader, Taxi and private hire driver, Landlord, Sole trader with employees.

    £20,000 for the 2026 to 2027 tax year, you will need to use it from 6 April 2028

    gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 30 October 2026

    you’re a sole trader or a landlord registered for Self Assessment

    gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 24 October 2026

Every year

  1. Income Tax quarterly updates

    Send an update for each quarter by its deadline. These are the standard update periods.

    Relevant for: Sole trader, Taxi and private hire driver, Landlord, Sole trader with employees.

    Standard update periods and deadlines
    Update period Deadline
    6 April to 5 July 7 August
    6 April to 5 October 7 November
    6 April to 5 January 7 February
    6 April to 5 April 7 May, in the following tax year

    6 April to 5 July 7 August 6 April to 5 October 7 November 6 April to 5 January 7 February 6 April to 5 April 7 May (the following tax year)

    gov.uk/guidance/use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax/send-quarterly-updates Retrieved 30 October 2026

  2. Income Tax final declaration

    Submit your tax return by 31 January following the end of the tax year. You can submit it earlier.

    Relevant for: Sole trader, Taxi and private hire driver, Landlord, Sole trader with employees.

    You must submit your tax return by 31 January following the end of the relevant tax year, but you can submit it earlier.

    gov.uk/guidance/use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax/submit-your-tax-return Retrieved 30 October 2026

  3. Companies House confirmation statement

    File at least one confirmation statement every 12 months, even if nothing has changed.

    Relevant for: Owner-managed company with one director, Property company, Small company.

    Optional: You can file early. You do not have to wait for the current review period to end.

    You must review your records and file at least one confirmation statement every 12 months.

    gov.uk/guidance/confirmation-statement-guidance Retrieved 24 October 2026

    You do not have to wait until your current review period has ended before filing your confirmation statement.

    gov.uk/guidance/confirmation-statement-guidance Retrieved 24 October 2026

  4. Companies House annual accounts

    File the annual accounts with Companies House 9 months after the end of the company's financial year.

    Relevant for: Owner-managed company with one director, Property company, Small company.

    Optional: You can file the accounts and the Company Tax Return together or separately.

    File annual accounts with Companies House 9 months after your company’s financial year ends

    gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company Retrieved 24 October 2026

    You can file with Companies House and HMRC together or separately.

    gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company Retrieved 24 October 2026

  5. Company Tax Return (CT600)

    File the Company Tax Return with HMRC 12 months after the end of the accounting period it covers.

    Relevant for: Owner-managed company with one director, Property company, Small company.

    The deadline for your tax return is 12 months after the end of the accounting period it covers.

    gov.uk/company-tax-returns/deadline-and-penalties Retrieved 24 October 2026

  6. Corporation Tax payment

    Pay Corporation Tax 9 months and 1 day after the end of the accounting period, when taxable profits are up to £1.5 million.

    Relevant for: Owner-managed company with one director, Property company, Small company.

    You must pay your Corporation Tax 9 months and 1 day after the end of your accounting period.

    gov.uk/pay-corporation-tax Retrieved 24 October 2026

No date yet

  1. Income Tax: partnerships

    Partnerships will use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax. HMRC has not yet set the date.

    Relevant for: Partnership.

    Partnerships will also need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax in the future. We’ll set out the timeline for this at a later date.

    gov.uk/guidance/find-out-if-and-when-you-need-to-use-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax Retrieved 30 October 2026
